messages:
jin: Heads-up — did a batch of AWQ conversions this morning for llama-2-13b (fp16 -> awq). Running group-size sweep (64/128/256/512) and toggling act-quant/act-order. Observing weird instability when serving under load (spikes, occasional NaNs)

maria: can you paste the exact conversion command? also which AWQ repo/version?

jin: sure — using awq v0.2.1 fork with our tiny patch. conversion command:```bash
python convert_awq.py --model-path /mnt/models/llama-2-13b/ --out awq/llama2-13b-awq --group-size 128 --act-quant True --act-order False --quantize-weights True
```

alex: quick q: act-quant True means we quantized activations to 8-bit symmetric, right? any change to fp16 KV cache?

jin: yes 8-bit activation quant (symmetric per-tensor fallback for small groups). KV cache still stored as fp16; conversion touches forward kernels only.

sara: summary of results? throughput / latency / quality deltas?

jin: short summary:
- group-size 64: stable under serving but very small accuracy delta (MMLU -0.6%) and throughput not great (+8% p50 token latency).
- group-size 128: sweet spot for local eval. MMLU -1.7%, HellaSwag -2.1%. Serving under our stress test (100 concurrent streams) OK for ~90s then occasional NaN on one worker (0.3% requests).
- group-size 256: throughput improved (~25% lower p50), MMLU -2.9%, HellaSwag -3.4%. NaN rate jumps to ~1.6% under sustained load.
- group-size 512: best throughput, MMLU -4.8%, but multiple workers hit instability within 30s.

maria: do we see the NaNs during generation or during a specific op (matmul, layernorm)? logs?

jin: from torch logs and core dumps: NaNs originate in fused attention matmul kernel on step N (varies). stack: atn_attn_matmul -> awq_quant_dot -> aten::linear. No explicit layernorm NaN. Repro on CPU doesn't happen; appears only on CUDA kernels.

alex: could be numerical overflow from act quant scaling mismatch. Did you try toggling act-order = True?

jin: yes. act-order True reduces NaN frequency by ~60% at group-size 256 (NaN -> 0.6%), but accuracy regressions slightly worse compared to act-order False. Seems act-order helps stability at cost of quant noise.

sara: any difference if we disable activation quant entirely and only quantize weights (pure AWQ weight-only)?

jin: weight-only AWQ (act-quant False) was very stable even at 512 but accuracy deltas are similar to group-size 128 weight+act, weirdly. So activations are the main instability contributor.

maria: do we have perf counters / fp-exceptions enabled? could we capture the tensor ranges pre/post quant to see overflow?

jin: enabled nvidia-smi dmon and CUPTI counters on a repro run. Also logged per-layer activation mins/maxes. In failing runs some attention heads show max activations 4-6x larger than baseline (due to softmax scaling / prompt lengths). When that happens combined with small act-scale (from small group quant) we see clipped values then NaN on matmul.

alex: possible mitigation: dynamic rescaling of act quant scales at runtime based on per-request percentile (e.g., 99.9th). Or fallback policy per-request: if max_act > threshold, mark request to use fp16 execution for a layer or whole request.

sara: we should add a graceful fallback: when we detect outlier activation ranges, route that request to a fp16 model variant or a model with larger group-size. We already have routing in the platform — can we wire a fast probe?

jin: I prototyped a tiny tracer inside serving runtime — it checks per-layer max during warmup tokens (first 16 tokens) and sets a flag. Pseudocode:```python
def warmup_check(tensor):
    if tensor.abs().max() > scale_threshold:
        request.meta["force_fp16"] = True
```
Works but adds ~1ms overhead per warmup token. Reduces NaN incidence to near-zero in our stress tests.

maria: how about model-level bakeoff numbers (latency / qps / cost delta) — we need them for doc to PMs.

jin: numbers from our 13B test harness (1x A100-40G equivalent):
- fp16 baseline: p50 token latency 48ms, qps 100, MMLU 72.4
- AWQ group64 (act-quant True): p50 52ms, qps 92, MMLU 71.8 (-0.6)
- AWQ group128 (act-quant True): p50 42ms, qps 118, MMLU 70.7 (-1.7)
- AWQ group256 (act-quant True): p50 36ms, qps 132, MMLU 69.5 (-2.9)
- AWQ group512 (act-quant True): p50 30ms, qps 160, MMLU 67.6 (-4.8)
Cost-per-token estimated drops ~25% @256 and ~40% @512 vs fp16 but QA risk increases.

alex: those tradeoffs look reasonable but we need clear SLOs: prefer group128 in default unless customer opts-in for aggressive perf. Add automatic fallbacks as safety net.

sara: agree. For Dedicated customers we can expose a profile: conservative (group64/act-quant False), balanced (group128/default), aggressive (group256/512 with opt-in + fallback enabled). Add a config toggle in Console + API.

maria: action items?

jin: 1) open PR to runtime: warmup-check + request-level fp16 fallback (I got prototype).
2) add per-model bakeoff doc (numbers above + HellaSwag, Winogrande) — I'll draft and put in model-onboarding repo.
3) run full MMLU sweep with more seeds to reduce noise and confirm deltas.
4) test AWQ v0.2.3 (upstream) for kernel fixes — might already address CUDA matmul corner case.

alex: i'll help with the Console toggles and add UI perms for Dedicated customers to opt-in.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime patch to canary cohort (platform/canary/awq-warmup-check) at 2024-06-07T18:00Z by jin

maria: thanks, this is super helpful. please attach the per-layer min/max logs and the small repro script to the PR so SRE can validate before canary. :thumbsup:
